summary:
[  edit  ]
The Laser  CHOP  produces channels that can drive a laser projector. It uses the points and lines of a  POP ,  SOP  or  CHOP  and outputs the channels at a specified sample rate, typically 10,000 to 96,000 samples per second. The Laser  CHOP  gives optimal control over the movement of the reflectors of the laser projector as well as enhanced color control. In particular, it gives better control of lines being straight, end-points being not cut off or over-drawn, and eliminating tails, all adjustable using a set of parameters.
When sending  CHOP  channels to the Laser  CHOP , the  CHOP  expects  x  and  y  channels and every sample will be interpreted as a point to be drawn. To draw multiple shapes, also specify a channel named  id  to identify each shape. Points with  id = 0  are part of the first shape, points with  id = 1  form the second shape. All other channels will be interpreted as color channels and blanking will be applied to those. This makes it possible to drive lasers that have more than just RGB diodes active.
The channels output from the Laser  CHOP  can be sent to the  Laser Device CHOP  in case of controlling a Laser via the  ILDA Protocol , or the  Audio Device Out CHOP  in case of using one of LaserAnimation Sollinger's  AVB  capable devices, where the audio is output via the  Audio Device Out CHOP  to a low-latency AVB-ready audio device like those from MOTU, RME, LaserAnimation Sollinger or Apple macOS.
LaserAnimation Sollinger's AVB2ILDA devices  give you access to features for the professional sector. See  Lasers .
The  CHOP  was developed with the help of  LaserAnimation Sollinger  who guided us in speccing and implementing the necessary parameters, especially in regards of the blanking timing settings.
Tip : See the  OP Snippets  for setup and usage examples.
(The Laser  CHOP  replaces the legacy Scan  CHOP .)
LASERS ARE DANGEROUS - DAMAGE TO YOUR OR THE AUDIENCE'S EYE SIGHT IS A VERY REAL RISK
If you plan to use lasers
Understand all the laws and regulations for laser operation in your area.
Become a certified Laser Safety Officer (this is required by law in some areas). Courses are available from ILDA directly:  ILDA Laser Safety Courses
Make sure an emergency stop button is close to you at all times.
Do not let anyone enter the laser projection area unless all precautions have been taken to limit the output.
Make sure there are no reflective surfaces in the projection area that might cause the beam to reflect unintendedly.
BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY (2025.30000):   The Laser  CHOP  was overhauled in 2025.30000 which includes many changes and additions from previous versions. Certain changes like the removal of Start Point Hold Time and Input Rate may cause output differences when loading older files into builds 2025.30000 or newer. The Input Rate parameter was previously used to define the sample rate during laser point generation, but that is now always done at 192000, followed by a resample to the Output Rate. This may require changes to parameters like Step Size or Blanking Step Size to achieve the same effect as in older versions.
Corner Points
The Laser  CHOP  categorizes input points as either corner points or guide points. Prior to the 2025.30000 series of builds, all points were considered corner points.
All input points are corner points by default. To set a point as either a corner or guide point, use a boolean attribute named  LasCorner  for  SOP /POP inputs, or a  lascorner  channel for  CHOP  inputs.  LasCorner = 1  means it is a corner point.
Guide points are simply points that help move the laser along a path or curve, and they will not have abrupt changes in line direction between the two line segments they're a part of. Guide points are only output once and never repeated. Guide points are also useful for point interpolation when stepping is done along the curve.
Corner points essentially define the start/end points of an individual line strip on the laser. Interpolation of color and point position stepping is done between corner points, with guide points used for weighting. Corner points should also be used when there is an abrupt change in the laser direction (eg. right or acute angle) so that appropriate hold points can be added to increase sharpness of the image.
Corner points repeat as a function of their angle and the corner hold parameters. Additionally, for extra per-point control, corner hold look-up factor and hold add can be used through special attributes in  SOP /POP inputs, or channels in  CHOP  inputs:
LasCornerHoldAdd  ( SOP  or  POP ) or  lascornerholdadd  ( CHOP )
LasCornerHoldLookupFactor  ( SOP  or  POP ) or  lascornerholdlookupfactor  ( CHOP )
Corner hold repeat is calculated as follows, where H is the hold value calculated from the angle/parameters:
NumRepeatPoints = HoldAdd + HoldLookupFactor * H
Blanking
Blanking is the capability of a laser projector to rapidly turn on / off the laser when displaying animations. For example when displaying multiple shapes, the laser  needs the ability of blanking to omit the empty spots between the shapes. Blanking is done automatically between shapes but quantity of blanking points is controlled through the set of blanking delay parameters on the Color Page, as well as the Blanking Step Size parameter on the Scanning Page.
As the laser's mirrors are driven by motors, the positional data that is send to the laser is likely to be ahead of the actual mirror position - the mirror must catch up to the data. The Color data though is in time and as a result the effect can be visible tails at points where the laser switches off its color. Adjusting the blanking parameters can help prevent this.
See also:  Laser Device CHOP ,  Pangolin CHOP ,  Line Smooth POP

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When disabled, the  CHOP  will zero out all channels.

parameters.label: Source  OP
parameters.name: source
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select the source operator type for the laser image.

parameters.label: SOP
parameters.name: sop
parameters.description: Use a  SOP  as the source for the Laser image. Apart from position attributes, the  SOP 's point color attributes are used to determine the color output.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Use a  CHOP  as the source for the Laser image. Tthe  CHOP  expects  x  and  y  channels and every sample will be interpreted as a point to be drawn. To draw multiple shapes, also specify a channel named  id  to identify each shape. Points with  id = 0  are part of the first shape, points with  id = 1  form the second shape. All other channels will be interpreted as color channels and blanking will be applied to those. This makes it possible to drive lasers that have more than just RGB diodes active.

parameters.label: POP
parameters.name: pop
parameters.description: Use a POP as the source for the Laser image. Apart from position attributes, the  POP 's color attributes are used to determine the color output.

parameters.label: SOP
parameters.name: sop
parameters.description: Path  to the  SOP . The  SOP 's position and color attributes (as well as other miscellaneous attributes such as  LasCorner ) will be used to generate the laser points.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: chop
parameters.description: Path  to the  CHOP . The input  CHOP  must have  x ,  y  channels for the point positions. In addition, it also supports  z ,  r ,  g ,  b , and  id  channels. The  id  channel is used for grouping points together as a single shape. By default when no  id  channel is present, each point is separate and unconnected. Additional and arbitrarily named colour channels may be added for laser projectors that accept more than just r, g, b. Additional channels include: "lascorner", "lascornerholdadd", and "lascornerholdlookupfactor".

parameters.label: POP
parameters.name: pop
parameters.description: Path  to the  POP . The  POP 's position and color attributes (as well as other miscellaneous attributes such as  LasCorner ) will be used to generate the laser points.

parameters.label: Output  Sample Rate
parameters.name: outputrate
parameters.description: The sample rate of the Laser  CHOP , and the sample rate at which it will output to the laser. With the default 48000 samples per second and a 60fps frame rate, the Laser  CHOP  can output 800 position and color values per frame.

parameters.label: Swap Output
parameters.name: swap
parameters.description: Lets you swap the x and y axis of the output.

parameters.label: X Scale
parameters.name: xscale
parameters.description: Control the horizontal scale of the output.

parameters.label: Y Scale
parameters.name: yscale
parameters.description: Control the vertical scale of the output.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: rotate
parameters.description: Control the rotation of the output.

parameters.label: Camera
parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: Specify the path to a Camera  COMP  used to draw a  SOP  from the cameras view.

parameters.label: Update Method
parameters.name: updatemethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - Control how the Laser  CHOP  pulls data from its source.

parameters.label: When All Points Drawn
parameters.name: alldrawn
parameters.description: The Laser  CHOP  will read the source data once all points of the previous frame have been drawn.

parameters.label: Every  Frame
parameters.name: everyframe
parameters.description: The Laser  CHOP  will update the input every frame, no matter if it finished drawing the previous frame or not.

parameters.label: Frame Start  Pulse
parameters.name: startpulse
parameters.description: When enabled, will insert a sample with all colors set to -1 at the beginning of the laser frame.

parameters.label: Debug  Channel
parameters.name: debugchan
parameters.description: When enabled, an extra channel with point state will be included:

parameters.label: Corner  Attribute  Name
parameters.name: cornerattr
parameters.description: For  SOP  and POP inputs, optionally change the point attribute name used to specifiy if a point is a corner point. Default is  LasCorner .

parameters.label: Corner Hold Add  Attribute  Name
parameters.name: cornerholdaddattr
parameters.description: For  SOP  and POP inputs, optionally change the name of the point attribute used to add a constant value to the corner hold time. Default is  LasCornerHoldAdd .

parameters.label: Corner Hold Factor  Attribute  Name
parameters.name: cornerholdfactorattr
parameters.description: For  SOP  and POP inputs, optionally change the name of the point attribute used to apply a lookup factor to the corner point hold. Default is  LasCornerHoldLookupFactor .

parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.name: stepsize
parameters.description: The distance each x,y can change while outputting color.

parameters.label: Blanking Step Size
parameters.name: bstepsize
parameters.description: The distance each x,y can change while not outputting color (blanking).

parameters.label: Minimum Corner Hold
parameters.name: mincornerhold
parameters.description: The minimum value of the corner hold of a point. The value of the corner hold of a point is calculated linearly in the range from the minimum to maximum corner hold, based on the steepness of the angle at the point. This angle is calculated with the following three points: the previous point, the point itself, and the next point. Example: when the angle at the point is 180 degrees then the corner hold of the point will be the minimum value.

parameters.label: Maximum Corner Hold
parameters.name: maxcornerhold
parameters.description: The maximum value of the corner hold of a point. See Minimum corner Hold for more details. When the angle at the point is 0 degrees, then the corner hold will be the maximum value. If the maximum value is lower than the minimum then the maximum will be clamped upward.

parameters.label: Corner Hold Lookup  CHOP
parameters.name: cornerholdchop
parameters.description: Reference  to a  CHOP  to use as the custom lookup curve when interpolating from min to max hold. By default (ie. when no  CHOP  is specified), then it is linearly interpolated.

parameters.label: Closed Shape Overlap
parameters.name: closedoverlap
parameters.description: For closed shapes, the number of points (specified in milliseconds) to overlap the start/end, to utilize color interpolation and get a more uniform shape.

parameters.label: Red Scale
parameters.name: redscale
parameters.description: Set the intensity of the Red  Channel .

parameters.label: Green Scale
parameters.name: greenscale
parameters.description: Set the intensity of the Green  Channel .

parameters.label: Blue Scale
parameters.name: bluescale
parameters.description: Set the intensity of the Blue  Channel .

parameters.label: Pre Blanking On Delay
parameters.name: preblankon
parameters.description: Set the time in ms the Laser should wait at a position before turning the color output off.

parameters.label: Post Blanking On Delay
parameters.name: postblankon
parameters.description: Set the time in ms the Laser should wait at a position after turning the color output off.

parameters.label: Pre Blanking Off Delay
parameters.name: preblankoff
parameters.description: Set the time in ms the Laser should wait at a position before turning the color output on.

parameters.label: Post Blanking Off Delay
parameters.name: postblankoff
parameters.description: Set the time in ms the Laser should wait at a position after turning the color output on.

parameters.label: Start-Point Hold Time
parameters.name: starthold
parameters.description: Set the time in ms the Laser should wait at the first point of a new data frame before continuing on.

parameters.label: Color Delay
parameters.name: colordelay
parameters.description: Set the delay in ms of the color channels in the output.

parameters.label: Interpolate Colors
parameters.name: interpcolors
parameters.description: When enabled, interpolates colors between points.

parameters.label: Brightness Curve Lookup  CHOP
parameters.name: brightnesscurvechop
parameters.description: Reference  a  CHOP  to use as a custom look-up for soft-edge blending of closed shapes.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter
parameters.name: autoname
parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: To "pulse" a parameter is to send it a signal from (1) an  exported  CHOP channel or (2) a python command or (3) a mouse click that causes a new action to occur immediately. A pulse via python is via the  .pulse()  function on a pulse
parameters.description: type parameter, such as Reset parameter in a  Speed CHOP . A pulse from a CHOP is typically a 0 to 1 to 0 signal in an exported channel.

parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

localNotes.excerpt: n informative workshop. POPs create and modify 3D data, replacing the older SOPs (Surface Operators) with enhanced performance and flexibility. ## 1. What are POPs? - **Definition**: POPs (Point Operators) are a family of operators in TouchDesigner that run on the GPU, leveraging high parallelism to create and manipulate 3D data efficiently. - **Purpose**: They generate and modify points, primitives, and attributes for rendering (via Render TOP) or output to external devices like LED arrays or lasers. - **Significance**: POPs replace SOPs with GPU acceleration, memory optimization, and integration with modern workflows (e.g., USD, FBX). ## 2. Core Components ### Points - Every POP contains a set of points with attributes. - **Key Attribute**: `P` (Position), a 3D vector (float3) defining a point’s location. - **Other Attributes**: Include `Color` (float4: red, green, blue, alpha), `Normal (N)` (float3), and user-defined attributes. ### Primitives - **Types**: - **Point**: 1 point. -
